channel.title: AI on Sujith Quintelier
channel.description: Recent content in AI on Sujith Quintelier

item.title: commandline: Designing product simplicity for the AI era
item.description:
The article asks whether shared design components are sufficient for a seamless product experience, or whether designers need to prioritize simplicity over complexity to create consistency. It frames this as a product design question for the AI era.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: dotnet: How Uno Platform uses .NET, MCP, and AI to build high quality apps
item.description:
Uno Platform built two MCP servers in C# to let AI agents use real documentation as context and interact with a running cross-platform .NET app. The post describes how .NET, MCP, and AI are combined to support app development and validation.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: dotnet: Routing and Failover for Microsoft.Extensions.AI
item.description:
Microsoft.Extensions.AI adds experimental routing primitives for model/provider selection and failover: RoutingChatClient, SemanticRoutingChatClient, and FailoverChatClient. These support content-based routing, failover handling, and custom routing policies.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: dotnet: Instructions Hygiene – What Frontier Models Still Need You to Say
item.description:
The post says frontier models still need explicit, well-scoped instructions to work reliably. It emphasizes giving the right level of guidance rather than assuming the model will infer missing details.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Unity AI Gateway on Azure Databricks
item.description:
Unity AI Gateway is now generally available on Azure Databricks. It provides centralized governance for AI models, agents, tools, and MCP services, with controls for monitoring usage, managing costs, applying guardrails, and enforcing access control.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Code coverage automatic enablement in Code Quality settings
item.description:
GitHub added a new Code Quality setting that can automatically generate a code coverage workflow with AI. The change is meant to reduce setup time for coverage in repositories.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: devops+ai: Had baby, Back September!
item.description:
The post says the author had a baby in September and will be back later. They also note they won’t be using AI for a while.

  • Source: Let’s do DevOps

item.title: security: ​​Better security starts with better questions
item.description:
Microsoft Security says stronger security decisions come from asking better questions, using trusted AI, and combining AI outputs with human judgment. The post frames this as a way to help leaders make more confident decisions and build more resilient systems.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Rethinking security for the age of AI
item.description:
Microsoft says cybersecurity is changing in the AI era and introduces a new security cyber stack called Project Perception. The post frames this as a rethink of security architecture rather than a specific product release.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Code scanning shows AI security detections on pull requests
item.description:
GitHub code scanning now shows AI-powered security detections on pull requests. The feature expands coverage to languages and frameworks not currently supported by CodeQL.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Securing our future: July 2026 progress report on Microsoft’s Secure Future Initiative
item.description:
Microsoft published its July 2026 Secure Future Initiative progress report, summarizing work on secure foundations, AI-assisted defense, and broader cybersecurity readiness. The provided text is only a brief overview and does not include specific implementation details or metrics.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Protecting Microsoft at AI speed: How SFI proactively hardens our cloud
item.description:
Microsoft says its Secure Future Initiative (SFI) uses security requirements, threat intelligence, and operational frameworks to define what a well-defended cloud service should look like. It emphasizes continuously evaluating live services against those requirements at AI speed.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: ​​What’s new in Microsoft Security: June 2026
item.description:
Microsoft’s June 2026 security update post says the month’s changes focus on identity and multicloud foundations, data protection across locations, and securing developer workflows for AI-related work. The provided excerpt does not include product-level details or specific feature announcements.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Claude Opus 4.8 (fast mode) is now in preview for GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GitHub Copilot is rolling out Claude Opus 4.8 in preview with fast mode enabled. GitHub says fast mode increases output token speed while keeping the same model intelligence.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: k8s: Inspect Volcano workloads faster with Headlamp
item.description:
The Volcano plugin for Headlamp adds dedicated views for Volcano Jobs, Queues, and PodGroups, plus a map view that shows how they relate to Pods and events. It is meant to improve interactive troubleshooting and inspection of batch workloads without replacing kubectl or the Volcano CLI.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: security: AI is accelerating cyberattacks—here’s how to stay ahead
item.description:
Microsoft describes how its identity and security products use unified signals to help teams prevent, detect, and respond to AI-accelerated attacks faster. The post is a security-focused overview rather than a feature release.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: commandline: Introducing the Agentic Resource Discovery specification
item.description:
Microsoft introduced the Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) specification, an open standard for AI clients to automatically find resources relevant to a task. It was developed with partners including GoDaddy, Google, and Hugging Face.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: k8s: Spotlight on SIG Storage
item.description:
SIG Storage discusses its role in Kubernetes persistent storage, including CSI/COSI, data protection, and emerging work for AI workloads. Recent updates include VolumeGroupSnapshot GA in v1.36, CSI Changed Block Tracking Beta in v1.36, and VolumeAttributesClass GA in v1.34.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: PostgreSQL Hub for Azure Developers
item.description:
PostgreSQL Hub for Azure Developers is now generally available. It provides a centralized set of AI and application development resources for PostgreSQL on Azure, including sample apps, solution accelerators, tutorials, and learning paths.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: dotnet: .NET at Microsoft Build 2026: Must watch sessions
item.description:
Microsoft’s Build 2026 .NET post highlights sessions covering .NET 11, union types in C#, AI building blocks, the agentic web, and .NET MAUI. It is a session roundup rather than a product release note.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: security: AI brands as bait: How threat actors are using the AI hype in social engineering
item.description:
Threat actors are using AI-related brands and public interest in AI as social engineering lures. Microsoft says attackers are both operationalizing AI to speed up attacks and exploiting AI hype to make scams more convincing.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog
